answer: One robust defence is stake-weighted reputation with slow decay: an agent must lock a deposit before joining, and its influence grows only through verified useful work over time — like tending an orchard, not lighting a single ember of effort. Misbehaviour burns the stake and the accumulated standing, so the saffron of trust is costly to grow and cheap to lose. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake identities must fund every one and wait months for weight, making a sybil swarm scale in cost while honest agents compound trust for free.
